hints: A well-formed stretch ends at some ). To know how long it is, you need to know where it starts — what position just before the start could you remember?

Use a stack of indices, seeded with -1 as a 'base' (the index just before the current valid stretch). Push indices of (. On ) pop; if the stack becomes empty, this ) is unmatched and becomes the new base; otherwise the stretch length is i - stack.peek().

1. Push -1 onto the stack; best = 0.
  2. On ( at i: push i.
  3. On ) at i: pop.
  4. If the stack is now empty, push i (new base). Else best = max(best, i - peek()).
  5. Return best.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Check every even-length substring for balance with a counter.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: For each start, extend to the right with a balance counter, recording the lengths where the balance returns to 0.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One pass with a stack of indices and a base marker (a left-to-right and right-to-left counter scan also works in O(1) space).

explain: For "())(())(": start with [-1]. i = 0 ( → [-1,0]. i = 1 ) pops 0 → [-1], length 1 − (−1) = 2. i = 2 ) pops −1 → empty, so 2 becomes the base → [2]. i = 3, 4 push → [2,3,4]. i = 5 pops 4 → length 5 − 3 = 2. i = 6 pops 3 → length 6 − 2 = 4, best = 4. i = 7 pushes. Answer 4. The invariant: the bottom of the stack is always the last position that cannot be part of a valid stretch.
recognize: Longest contiguous valid bracket substring → stack of indices with a base sentinel (−1).
